This Petition Coming On For Orders This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 Oral Order
(Per: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Singh Yerur)

This is an unfortunate case of 17 years old young female teenager, whose parents are before this Court seeking permission for medical termination of pregnancy of their daughter, a spine chilling and heart wrenching tale of 17 years old girl who is the daughter of petitioners.
Petitioners' daughter was taken to the Hospital complaining about her irregular menstrual cycle, during which time shockingly petitioners came to know about the pregnancy of their minor daughter.

Petitioners lodged a complaint before the Adur Police Station in Crime No.183/2024 against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 4, 6, 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Sections 376(2)(n),
506 of IPC (section NC: 2024:KHC-D:18063 64(2)(m), 351 of BNS, 2023).

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Pursuant to clinical check up and treatment, it was revealed to the petitioners that their minor daughter (victim girl-X) is 27 weeks and 21 days of pregnant gestation.
Daughter of the petitioners is 17 years old.

2. In view of unforeseen, unwanted pregnancy the minor girl is not willing to beget the child at this stage and considering her age and health condition, petitioners have filed this petition seeking permission of this Court to abort the feotus by way of medical termination of pregnancy (MTP).

sentences.text: this context, the petitioners approached the 3rd respondent-Child Welfare Committee, Haveri District for conducting MTP, which was rejected.
Hence, the petitioners are before this Court.

The victim minor girl (X) is school going and the petitioners are her parents and they do not want their daughter to beget the child which is forced on her without consent of the petitioner inflicted on the young school going child.

Petitioners have relied on the Judgment of this Court in identical case in Writ Petition No.105785/2024 (GM- RES), wherein similar situation this Court had permitted the medical termination of pregnancy (MTP).

Learned counsel for the petitioners has also relies on the Judgment rendered in the case of Meera Santosh Pal and Others vs. Union of India and Others,
reported in (2017) 3 SCC 462 by the Hon'ble Apex Court, wherein it is held in the report of the board that continuing pregnancy will cause more mental anguish, more pain and agony.

sentences.text: Hence, the present petition is filed.

4. This Court upon hearing the learned counsel for the petitioners, vide order dated 09.12.2024 directed the 2nd respondent to constitute a committee for considering the case of the minor girl of 17 years age for undergoing medical termination of pregnancy and furnish report accordingly.

In compliance of the said order passed by this Court, the learned AGA filed a memo along with the report of the Medical Board, whereby the medical board has certified the NC: 2024:KHC-D:18063 minor victim girl (X) to be fit to undergo MTP by its report dated 10.12.2024.

5. Having considered the report, this Court is of the opinion that in the interest of the minor victim girl, her health, future and the condition in which the petitioners and minor victim girl are living, it would be better to accept the Medical Board's report and to permit the minor victim girl (X) to undergo medical termination of pregnancy (MTP).

6 . Under the circumstances, taking all these facts into consideration and the medical report furnished by the Medical Board, this Court accepts the argument put forth by the learned counsel for the petitioners for granting permission to the petitioners to get the medical termination of pregnancy of their minor girl aged 17 years.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Petition is allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:18063 ii) Petitioners are permitted to terminate ongoing pregnancy of his minor daughter (X)/ victim girl through respondent No.2.
iii) Respondent No.2 is directed to conduct medical termination of pregnancy of the petitioners'
daughter (victim girl-X) as per report by the Medical Board dated 10.12.2024 in accordance to the Shabbirahammad S/O Gosumiddinsab ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33680323/
3 provisions of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971.
iv) It is further directed, upon termination of pregnancy, respondent No.2 shall ensure that the foetus/abortus is preserved for DNA test, if terminated.
v) Copy of this order shall be furnished to the petitioners and respondents forthwith for immediate and suitable action.
vi) It is needless to mention that proper, suitable medical care and attention shall be given to NC:
2024:KHC-D:18063 the patient i.e., daughter of the petitioners while performing MTP.
